newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Express May load factor up.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Express May load factor up.

text.p: Midwest Express Holdings Inc said Tuesday its Midwest Express Airlines's load factor in May rose 1.3 percentage points to 64.5 percent from 63.2 percent a year ago.
Its Skyway Airlines' May load factor fell 1.9 points to 45.2 percent from 47.1 percent.

Midwest Express' revenue passenger miles in the month gained 16.8 percent to 119.4 million from 102.2 million, while Skyway's revenue passenger miles dropped 10.9 percent to 5.7 million from 6.4 million, it said.
Midwest Express' available seat miles in May rose 14.4 percent to 185.0 million from 161.7 million, while Skyway's dropped 7.3 percent to 12.6 million from 13.6 million.
"May was another strong traffic month for Midwest Express. We boarded 10 percent more passengers than last year at this time," Timothy Hoeksema, chairman, said in a statement.

He attributed the increase to new service introduced during the month between Kansas City, Mo., and New York's La Guardia Airport, as well as service expansions between Boston and Kansas City and between Milwaukee and Orlando.

Skyway's May results were hurt by the pulldown of service between Detroit and Rockford, Ill., the company said. In late June, Skyway will begin nonstop service between Milwaukee and Marquette, Mich., and enhance service between Milwaukee and both Lansing, Mich., and Cincinnati, it added.
